decision: D-023 (was O-11 and O-12): install, install --repair, upgrade and uninstall say what they will do and ask for confirmation (--yes skips; --dry-run reports only); any git hook written, replaced (edited or not) or removed is listed in that plan. Exception: automatic setup (first tool/hook run after a PM install moved the pin) needs no approval, refreshes Directive's hooks with the rest of the wiring locally, and names what it updated. O-11: an edited Directive git hook is replaced and named ('Updated <path>; your earlier version is in git history'); a hook that isn't Directive-shaped stays a named conflict, untouched. O-12: automatic setup refreshes committed git hooks; a person commits them. #5859's keep-any-differing-hook rule is removed.
